        "id": "arc_template_stamping_infer_anchor_copy_and_validate",

        "title": "ARC template stamping: infer anchor, copy, and validate",
        "content": "For recurring ARC tasks with a small multicolor object and isolated marker cells, use demos to infer the object's bounding box and which point in it aligns with each marker. Replace each marker with a translated copy of the object, preserve the original object unless demos indicate otherwise, and clip copies at grid boundaries. Determine overlap behavior from examples rather than assuming it. Generate the output programmatically when possible and validate that it has the intended dimensions and every row has equal width before submission.",

      "arc_template_stamping_verify_placement_rule_before_broad_stamping": {
        "id": "arc_template_stamping_verify_placement_rule_before_broad_stamping",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC template-stamping: verify placement rule before broad stamping",
        "content": "For ARC puzzles with a small colored motif embedded in a noisy two-color grid, demos may show the motif copied onto matching background-color patterns, but do not assume simple runs of the dominant or minority color are targets. Check each demo by locating the exact copied motif, testing candidate placements against the original cells, and accounting for rotations/reflections and overlaps. In a 2026-09-29 task (30x17, 5/0 field, vertical three 1s), repeated guesses stamping on vertical 5 triples, vertical 0 triples, and horizontal/vertical runs were all wrong. Therefore compare every demonstrated placement and infer the precise match condition before submitting; request demos when uncertainty outweighs their cost.",

      "arc_colored_shape_stencil_matching_zero_patterns": {
        "id": "arc_colored_shape_stencil_matching_zero_patterns",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC colored-shape stencil matching zero patterns",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a noisy two-color background and a small connected non-background colored motif, treat the motif’s occupied cells as a stencil, not as a run-length threshold. Enumerate translations for which every occupied stencil coordinate overlaps a background cell (often 0 in demonstrations). Compute all matches against the original grid before painting; recolor the union of matched stencil cells with the motif color so overlaps do not suppress later matches. Preserve the source motif and all other cells. Infer the background and motif colors from the task examples, and verify the placement rule against the demonstrations before applying it broadly. This rule solved task-6508a967, whose motif was a 3-cell L and whose demos used other small motifs.",

        "title": "ARC: fill fully enclosed outline regions with the demonstrated fill color",
        "content": "For ARC grids with background cells bounded by an outline or line network, identify genuinely enclosed regions and fill their interior with the color demonstrated by input-output examples. Do not assume the fill color is the outline color or the original background. In task-a45610b3, a demo established color 4 as the fill color: the test contained a color-7 rectangular boundary around color-5 cells, and changing only those interior cells to 4 solved it. Preserve the boundary and all unbounded background; use demonstrations to determine which enclosed regions qualify and the fill color.",

      "arc_recolor_matching_shapes_among_scattered_objects_unresolved": {
        "id": "arc_recolor_matching_shapes_among_scattered_objects_unresolved",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC recolor matching shapes among scattered objects (unresolved)",
        "content": "Evidence from several demonstrations: these ARC tasks contain scattered colored components on a uniform background and outputs selectively recolor a component while preserving geometry. In demos, changed objects included (a) a 3-pixel L of color 6 to 0, (b) a two-pixel color-8 vertical pair to 2, (c) part/component of color 1 to 5, (d) a 4-pixel stair-like color-1 component to 2, (e) a large color-7 block to 2, (f) a color-5 component to 6, and (g) a color-6 component whose shape duplicated a color-8 component to color 1. Do not assume the rule is simply nearest component, duplicated shape, or recolor to the largest object color: multiple such guesses failed on a test containing a color-0 3x3 motif, color-2 large L, color-8 components, color-3 components, and a color-4 singleton. Infer the mapping from all demonstrations before submitting; preserve exact grid dimensions/rows and validate JSON grid shape.",

      "arc_fill_outlined_rectangular_cavities_even_when_outlines_are_open": {
        "id": "arc_fill_outlined_rectangular_cavities_even_when_outlines_are_open",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC fill outlined rectangular cavities even when outlines are open",
        "content": "Evidence from task-a45610b3 demos: several ARC inputs contain sparse orthogonal line outlines in one color on a solid background. Output changes selected interior background cells to color 4 while preserving outline/background. Rectangles may be closed by the grid boundary or formed by adjoining line segments; examples fill interiors of rectangular cavities of varying dimensions (including thin 1xN and 2x3). Do not assume every apparent pocket is enclosed: test pairs show fills only in specific cavities where borders are complete, including grid edge as a border. This task instance remained unsolved; test had a complex zigzag outline, and multiple guessed cavities were wrong. Future instances: derive exact wall geometry from demos, enumerate bounded background regions by flood fill treating grid edge as potential wall only when line segments close the other boundaries; validate the proposed rule against all demo outputs before submitting.",

        "title": "ARC open rectangular cavity fill color 4",
        "content": "Validated on task-a45610b3 across two demo pairs and a test: grids have a uniform background and thin orthogonal outline/line structures in a second color. In the demos, multiple rectangles could be filled; a separate shape with an incomplete boundary had its enclosed portion filled only where fully bounded, and exterior cells remained unchanged. Test succeeded by filling all enclosed interiors with 4. Important output: construct exact same dimensions and row widths; the first attempted response was rejected as invalid grid formatting, then corrected same rule and passed.",

        "title": "ARC demo-specific cellwise palette remapping",
        "content": "For ARC tasks where demos show a cellwise palette transformation, record the exact mapping for each demonstrated input palette pair; do not infer mappings from color frequency, dominance, or another pair. Observed examples: input colors {5,7} mapped 5→7 and 7→0; input colors {9,5} mapped 9→0 and 5→9. The {9,5} mapping correctly solved a test; an unsupported mapping of 9→7 and 5→0 was incorrect.         "id": "arc_l_marker_selects_a_component_to_recolor",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC L-marker selects a component to recolor",
        "content": "When a grid contains a long two-arm L-shaped marker in a distinct color, the output may recolor one scattered component to the marker color while preserving all other cells. In task-9c84caa6, demos had a color-2 L marker and changed a color-1 component, and a color-7 L marker and changed a color-2 component. Test marker was color 2 with vertical arm then horizontal arm right; the nearby 0-colored patch immediately left of the marker (rows 2-5, cols 16-18) was recolored to 2. This solved the instance. Selection rule is not fully determined by these examples; use demos and spatial relation to identify the target, and do not assume a fixed source color or alter unrelated components.",

      "arc_boundary_triggered_line_extension_and_marker_recoloring": {
        "id": "arc_boundary_triggered_line_extension_and_marker_recoloring",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC boundary-triggered line extension and marker recoloring",
        "content": "Observed recurring ARC pattern family (task-3d36488c): a uniform field, paired same-color cells on grid edges, and isolated colored cells. Demos show isolated markers often change to color 4 and extend line(s) of their original color toward aligned boundary/paired edge markers. Exact direction is task-dependent: in demo3, 5-pairs on top/bottom edges and a lone 0 at (1,4) yielded 0 down column 0 from top pair and 0 up column 4 from bottom pair; lone 0 became 4. Demo6: edge 5-stripes and isolated 1s cast horizontal/vertical rays of color 1 toward the 5 boundary, source becomes 4. Demo7: isolated 6 markers projected toward paired 5 boundary regions, source becomes 4, with projected fill color 6. Important caution: do not extrapolate beams from every pair automatically; deduce each marker direction and destination from alignments and demonstration geometry. This agent repeatedly guessed incorrectly on test with background 9, edge pairs of 0 at top cols 3-4 and bottom cols16-17, isolated 1 at (5,3); no correct output learned. Request demonstrations when edge alignment/direction is ambiguous, and validate each proposed ray against every demo before submitting.",

      "arc_scattered_shape_recoloring_from_matching_motif": {
        "id": "arc_scattered_shape_recoloring_from_matching_motif",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC scattered-shape recoloring from matching motif",
        "content": "Evidence from task-9c84caa6 (8 demos): Large grids contain scattered objects on a uniform background, with several palette colors. Demonstrations usually change one connected object (or one local blob) from its original color to a selected reference color, leaving dimensions and all else unchanged. Observed pair diffs: demo 3 recolored a small color-3 object to 6; demo 4 recolored a horizontal color-8 blob to 1; demo 5 recolored a color-0 blob to 5; demo 6 recolored one color-6 blob to 4; demo 7 recolored two color-5 cells to 8; demo 8 recolored a 3-cell color-0 L/tromino to 3. The demonstrations suggest shape/motif correspondence among scattered objects, but the exact selector was not confidently inferred in this instance. Avoid speculative full-grid submissions: compute exact input/output diffs for every demo, identify the changed object's shape and recolor, check whether it matches a motif/reference object (including rotations/reflections and component-vs-background connectivity), and only apply a well-supported correspondence to test. Preserve all unchanged cells and verify dimensions/row widths carefully. In task-9c84caa6, several guesses about which test component to recolor failed; later submissions also had invalid row widths. Do not infer the target merely by proximity to a large line or by choosing the largest component.",

Gather demos, record each panel’s marker coordinates/counts and output, then infer a positional/pattern predicate before submitting. Test instance 8x5 had 2x2 panels split by row/column color 9; each panel contained 2/3 colors, but all eight attempted outputs were incorrect.",

      "arc_three_by_two_row_reversal_tiling": {
        "id": "arc_three_by_two_row_reversal_tiling",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC 3H×2W tiling with reversed outer bands and mirrored left blocks",
        "content": "For ARC tasks whose demos expand an H×W input to 3H×2W, test whether each output row is made from two copies of an input row: a horizontally reversed copy on the left and the unchanged row on the right. The demonstrated vertical pattern was [input rows in reverse order, input rows in normal order, input rows in reverse order]. Thus output band b uses input row H−1−i for the outer bands and row i for the middle band, with output row [reverse(source_row) + source_row]. Do not assume all three bands have the same vertical ordering or infer the rule from dimensions alone: map several demo rows to input rows and verify all bands and both horizontal halves before applying it to a test.",

The vertical input-row index sequence is H−1..0, then 0..H−1, then H−1..0. Confirmed by task-a8a91d13: a 6×8 demo produced an 18×16 output with this rule; its 2×1 all-2 test produced a 6×2 all-2 grid. Verify horizontal orientation and band ordering from demonstrations before applying, since constant or symmetric inputs may not distinguish alternatives.",

Across five demonstrated pairs, cells outside that quadrant appear to be generated from the input palette, but no deterministic relationship to the input was established. Several guessed fills failed, including constant-background, checkerboard, and arbitrary binary fills. On recurrence, preserve the known top-left copy and do not present a guessed completion of the other quadrants as a validated rule.         "content": "For recurring task-9c84caa6 grids, demonstrations support selectively recoloring a component whose shape matches a conspicuous marker or divider structure, using the marker's color, while preserving unrelated cells and components. Infer from demos which matching occurrence is selected; do not recolor every congruent object or assume that a visually similar object is the target. Earlier guesses that recolored the color-3 object, changed the divider, or recolored the template itself were wrong.         "title": "ARC task-44d81bbe: preserve and replicate the centered source motif",

Preserve the original source motif in the output, then stamp its exact colored-cell pattern at every marker, aligning each marker with the center of the motif bounding box. Preserve grid dimensions and background; clip copies at grid edges if required. Validate the anchor and construction against demos before submitting.         "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC repeated lattice separators with encoded intersections (unresolved task-f39763d3)",
        "content": "Observed task-f39763d3 demos: grids consist of a solid field periodically traversed by one-cell horizontal and vertical separator lines. Separator intersections carry non-background symbols. Outputs are much smaller grids representing a compressed/selected lattice pattern, not simply all line-crossing colors: examples include 28x18 -> 1x1 [8], 28x29 -> 4x5, 30x18 -> 3x3, 29x30 -> 5x3. In one 29x30 example the output was [[8,8,4],[4,8,4],[4,4,8],[9,4,4],[9,9,9]], and source horizontal rows/vertical columns contained these symbols among regular background/line colors. The exact reduction rule was not resolved. On recurrence, request demos early and infer output crop/dimensions and sampling using several pairs; do not assume output is the raw intersection matrix or fill with the dominant color. Current test with background 3, horizontal separator rows 2 and 15, vertical separator cols 4,10,16,22, and 6 at four crossings was incorrectly answered after multiple guesses; no correct output established.",

        "id": "arc_task_12adf3d1_component_recoloring_unresolved",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC task-12adf3d1: localized component recoloring rule unresolved",
        "content": "Task-12adf3d1 remains unresolved. Across eight demos, grids have a uniform background, many disconnected multicolor motifs, and thin marker lines. Outputs preserve dimensions and almost all cells while locally recoloring an object or component. Observed changes: demo 1, a five-cell color-4 component became 3; demo 2, a singleton 3 became 5; demo 3, a singleton 4 became 6; demo 4, a color-7 component became 6; demo 5, a color-1 shape became 4; demo 6, a singleton 3 became 8; demo 7, a color-5 component became 3; demo 8, a two-cell color-3 component became 6. These examples do not reveal a dependable component-selection or replacement-color rule. Hypotheses based on recoloring identical-shape duplicates or simply changing an apparent repeated motif or line-shaped object were unreliable; all test submissions in the recorded instance were incorrect, so there is no test ground truth. On recurrence, compare demonstrations carefully to infer both which component is selected and its replacement color; do not guess from apparent shape repetition alone.",

      "task_12adf3d1_recoloring_unresolved_observed_demos_and_failed_heuristics": {
        "id": "task_12adf3d1_recoloring_unresolved_observed_demos_and_failed_heuristics",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "task-12adf3d1 recoloring unresolved: observed demos and failed heuristics",
        "content": "ARC task-12adf3d1 remains unresolved despite 8 demo requests and 8 wrong submissions. Demos consistently preserved almost all cells and recolored a small connected region into another existing color. Observed exact changes: Demo1 5-color component in upper-left corner changed to 6 (the other scattered 5 cells unchanged). Demo2 singleton 8 at row16,col11 (0-based row16? demo coordinates visually row17 col12) changed to 9; other objects unchanged. Demo3 two adjacent 0 cells near lower right changed to 4. Demo4 7 triplet at rows3, col19-21 changed to 8. Demo5 three 7s at right edge (row7 col25 and row8 col24-25) changed to3. Demo6 a 2x3 block of 2 at lower-left changed to5. Demo7 a central 8 component of roughly 8 cells changed to7. Demo8 adjacent horizontal pair of 5 changed to8. No coherent rule established.
